scenes.headline: Seven subsea cables come ashore at Mombasa.
scenes.footnote: All land at Mombasa; 2Africa also at Mtwapa · Africa-1 is landed, RFS pending · Source: DC254 cable tracker, verified Sep 2026

scenes.headline: Landing stations hand traffic to terrestrial fibre, into Nairobi.
scenes.footnote: Every node on this chain is tracked individually in the DC254 directory.

scenes.label: Networks peering at KIXP, hosted inside Nairobi's carrier-neutral data centres — 2,985 Gbps port capacity; KIXP peak: 1.3 Tbps (TESPOK, Jun 2024)
Operational data centres in Nairobi — where the exchanges and the carriers meet; 4 more operate in Mombasa

sourcePolicy: Relationship chain (Mombasa landings -> terrestrial fibre -> Nairobi hubs -> facilities) is animated as a schematic; the Kenya outline is generated from the open johan/world.geo.json dataset and node positions are real coordinates. Cable names, RFS years and landing sites: DC254 cable tracker, last verified Sep 2026 (2Africa also lands at Mtwapa; Africa-1 landed, RFS pending; Daraja announced and LuLu planned are excluded from the on-screen count of seven in-service systems). KIXP figures: PeeringDB KIXP profile (144 member networks, 2,985 Gbps port capacity, verified Oct 2026) and TESPOK historic peak 1.3 Tbps (25 Jun 2024), as cited in the validated DC254 KIXP explainer. Facility counts: DC254 directory 2026-Q3 dataset (13 operational Nairobi, 4 operational Mombasa). The map is a stylised schematic, not a routing map: no fibre routes, capacities or paths are drawn as fact beyond the Mombasa-Nairobi relationship the validated articles describe.
